findings.accepted_because: This compressed citation stands in settled prose untouched in iteration 4 (where only line 43 moved to replace a bare chronology reference), repairing it would reopen settled study prose and trigger unnecessary downstream re-reviews, and a reader is not misled about St. Leo's Advent teaching because Sermon 19.1 genuinely expounds Luke 21:34 against gluttony and worldly cares while Sermon 12.4 (already cited at sections/06-lane-conversion.tex:14, 41 and sections/09-references.tex:28) supplies the tenth-month triad of prayer, fasting, and almsgiving.
findings.problem: Line 30 cites St. Leo the Great's Sermon 19.1 alone for the Advent discipline 'fasting, prayer, and almsgiving keep the heart from being weighed down by gluttony and worldly cares before that sudden Day,' and line 45 (Moral sense) repeats 'prayer, fasting, and almsgiving ... (Rom. 13:13; Leo, Serm. 19.1).' Direct inspection of the bound checked passage (passage.nicene-and-post-nicene-fathers.series-2-volume-12.new-york-1895.leo-sermo-19.1) and the full CCEL text of Sermon XIX.1 (ccel-text-7bb1db6e) confirms that Sermon 19.1 expounds Luke 21:34 against gluttony, drunkenness, and worldly cares and commends bodily self-restraint without mentioning prayer or almsgiving (fasting and almsgiving appear in unbound sections XIX.2-3). The tenth-month triad 'prayer, fasting, and almsgiving' comes from bound Sermon 12.4 (leo-sermo-12.4.toml), which research/interpretations.md:24 cited beside 19.1 as '(Sermons 19.1, 12.4)' and sections/09-references.tex:28 already lists.
findings.required_result: If sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex is reopened in a future edit, cite both loci ('Sermon 19.1; cf. Sermon 12.4' at line 30 and 'Leo, Serm. 12.4, 19.1' at line 45) or narrow line 30 to Sermon 19.1's own call to self-restraint against gluttony and worldly cares.

findings.problem: Four passages name the secondary Douay-Rheims textual control 'the Challoner Gutenberg 1581 edition' (sections/02-appointed-text.tex:62; sections/03-detailed-commentary.tex:34) or 'the Challoner Gutenberg 1581 witness' (sections/08-scope.tex:10; sections/09-references.tex:16). Per edition.english-college-of-douay.douay-rheims-bible.challoner-gutenberg-1581 (edition.toml), '1581' is Project Gutenberg eBook number 1581 (released 1998 from Challoner's 1749-1752 revision), not a 1581 printing; placing 'Gutenberg 1581 edition' beside '1899 American Douay-Rheims edition' carries internal slug shorthand into reader prose and risks reading like a publication year (one year before the 1582 Rheims New Testament), though generated/scriptural-date-location.tex in the same study prints 'Project Gutenberg eBook 1581' unambiguously.
findings.required_result: In any future edit touching these passages, replace 'the Challoner Gutenberg 1581 edition' and 'the Challoner Gutenberg 1581 witness' with 'Project Gutenberg eBook 1581 of the Challoner revision' so the catalog number cannot be misread as a publication year.

summary: Independent cold review (iteration 4) of the canonical expansive study for Dominica prima Adventus in the 1962 Missale Romanum (src/gemini/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/01-first-sunday-of-advent: main.tex, publication.toml, proper-components.toml, web-edition.toml, generation-metadata.tex, and sections/01-opening.tex through sections/09-references.tex) against guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md, guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md, guidance/editorial.md, research records, and primary witnesses in src/sources/. Verdict: PASS (zero blocking findings; one accepted finding STU-012 and one advisory finding STU-013 in settled prose). Authorization (guidance/liturgy/propers-production-plan.md, 2026-11-25) and complete-text publication mode (appointed_text_completeness = "complete") agree across manifest, research, and prose; strict 1962 liturgical isolation is preserved; all carrying authors resolve with eligible standing in author-standing-v1.toml; and tools/tpt check-proper-components and check-content-preflight pass cleanly. All iteration-4 repairs within REVIEW_SCOPE are verified clean: all eight chronology cross-references now use explicit named links (\hyperref[sec:date-location]{\work{Scriptural Date and Location}}), all six liturgical rubric cues and the Introit repetition cue inside \begin{latinproper} use upright \textnormal{...}, and ellipsis spacing (\dots{}) is fixed with zero regressions. All ten appointed Latin/English proper texts and the Trinity Preface match their tracked Douay-Rheims 1899, Lasance/Walsh 1945, and collated Latin witnesses; no authored prose restates or contradicts dates in the generated Scriptural Date and Location appendix; Amalarius's 838 Kiersy censure and differing medieval Advent I Gospel assignments (Sicard, Rupert, Durandus) obey the liturgical-commentator rules; and reader register stays plain, source-grounded, and free of coverage roll calls or process narration. Consequential-difficulty tests verified directly at cited primary loci: (1) St. Ambrose of Milan, Expositio Evangelii secundum Lucam X.37-45 (book-10-html-083e1630; luke-21-29.toml) on Luke 21:27 (in nube) and Luke 21:29 (et omnes arbores) at sections/05-lane-incarnational.tex:10-16 — PASS: the prose teaches both textual questions before resolving them, follows Ambrose's exact inferences via Isa 19:1 and Luke 1:35 (Mary as the light cloud overshadowed by the Spirit) and X.44-45 (Israel and Gentile nations blossoming toward resurrection harvest vs. barren leaves of Gen 3:7), and clearly contrasts the consequence with Gregory's ironic fructus mundi ruina est; (2) St. Bede, In Lucae Evangelium Expositio VI on Luke 21:33 (luke-21-33.toml) alongside St. Augustine, De civitate Dei XX.14, 16, 24 (ccel-text-5c973fed) at sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex:22-24 — PASS: the prose faithfully distinguishes Bede's direct Luke 21:33 resolution (aereum vs. aethereum sive sidereum; per imaginem vs. per essentiam reconciling Luke 21:33 with Eccl 1:4; per ignem tergetur) from Augustine's underlying arguments in XX.14 (Apoc 20:9-13, 1 Cor 7:31-32), XX.16 (Apoc 21:1), and XX.24 (Ps 101:26-28, Matt 24:35, 2 Pet 3:6-11). Offline/remote research bounds (restricted 2026 institutional Ordo HTML payloads, RG 128 Latin text, Murphy 1914, Greek Psalmaries, Hilary, Cassiodorus, Augustine Ep. 199, Aquinas on Romans) remain honestly disclosed in sections/08-scope.tex and research/scope.md.
